Result.Name: Approval Expired
Result.Description: Status used if the cases' approval time period has expired (i.e. the Standard Building Plan approval may only be good for 3 years). EnerGov's IAA will set the case status to this automatically when the approval expire date equals the current date

Result.Name: Approved
Result.Description: Status used if the review is approved, and the appeal period has passed

Result.Name: Denied
Result.Description: Status used if the application has been denied

Result.Name: In Appeal Period
Result.Description: Status used following the initial approval.  After an application has been decided on by staff, planning commission or council, the public and applicant have a period of time to appeal the decision

Result.Name: In Review
Result.Description: Status applied to a case when the review is in progress

Result.Name: On Hold
Result.Description: Status used if the case is on hold for any reason

Result.Name: Review Expired
Result.Description: Status used for cases where the review period has expired.  If a case should reach a decision in 6 months, but hasn't, the case status will be changed to this by EnerGov's IAA

Result.Name: Submitted
Result.Description: Status used as the default status for most cases, before the review begins

Result.Name: Submitted - Online
Result.Description: Status that online applications should inherit when first submitted

Result.Name: Void
Result.Description: Status used if the plan case has been cancelled and no further review will be conducted

Result.Name: Withdrawn
Result.Description: Status used if the applicant has withdrawn the application (i.e. following a pre-application meeting)
